course_profile.one_sentence_summary: An applied Python-centered NLP course that moves from text acquisition and preprocessing to semantic analysis and introductory neural methods, with progressive laboratory implementation tasks and a project practicum.
course_profile.short_summary: The course is positioned as a continuation of Data Science and is designed to develop the ability to synthesize and verify mathematical models and build specialized software for natural language processing. The accessible materials show a progressive structure: text acquisition and filtering, tokenization and normalization, vectorization and POS analysis, frequency/probabilistic and semantic analysis, classification, similarity, sentiment, and neural-network-based text analysis; the official syllabus then extends this trajectory into audio, GPT-supported NLP, and a project practicum, although those later source documents were not uploaded.

source_coverage.coverage_comment: Analysis used the official syllabus, laboratory works 1-6, and lectures 1-11. The syllabus also lists later topics and labs on audio messages, GPT-supported NLP, and global information space, but those source documents were not uploaded, so they are treated as scope-level topics rather than strongly evidenced output skills.

Differentiate tokenization, stop-word removal, lemmatization, stemming, vectorization, POS tagging, clustering, classification, similarity analysis, and sentiment analysis.
Describe the role of artificial neural network architectures in NLP, including feedforward, recurrent, LSTM/GRU, CNN, and transformer-based approaches.

Implement end-to-end workflows for vectorization, POS-aware analysis, clustering, classification, text similarity, and sentiment analysis.
Prototype introductory neural-network-based solutions for text comparison and sentiment-related tasks on domain-specific corpora.

Verify correctness of script implementations and compare alternative technologies or approaches when required by the assignment format.
Assess whether extracted keywords, clusters, or sentiment outputs are aligned with the underlying topic or domain.

curricular_relations.from_label: Text Data Collection via Web Scraping
curricular_relations.reason: The course sequence starts with acquiring text data and then filtering or cleaning that collected text before further NLP processing.
Lecture and lab workflows present filtering and normalization as early preprocessing steps before token-level operations.
Stop-word removal depends on having tokenized text units.
The preprocessing pipeline groups tokenization with later normalization steps such as lemmatization.
The lab workflow treats stemming as a downstream operation applied to tokenized text.
Normalized lexical forms make top-word and frequency analysis more interpretable across text variants.
Clustering methods in the course depend on transforming text into machine-usable representations.
Lecture materials frame text classification as a machine-learning task over represented text features.
Similarity analysis is taught through vector representations such as cosine-based comparisons and sentence embeddings.
Lecture 10 presents sentiment analysis as classification of text according to emotional tone or polarity.
The lecture materials explicitly connect similarity, classification, and sentiment as related analytical processes.
The deep-learning lab requires applying neural methods to comparative content analysis and similarity-oriented tasks.
The deep-learning lab explicitly asks students to perform sentiment analysis using neural networks.

evidence.claim: The official scope spans classical NLP preprocessing, semantic analysis, deep learning, and a later project practicum.
evidence.source_title: Силабус Аналіз та обробка природньої мови (NLP) 2025.pdf
evidence.evidence_text: The syllabus lists modules on introduction/data acquisition, preprocessing and syntactic analysis, semantic analysis, deep learning for NLP, and a project practicum, including later audio, GPT, and global information space topics.

evidence.claim: The course is explicitly applied and Python-centered.
evidence.source_title: Силабус Аналіз та обробка природньої мови (NLP) 2025.pdf
evidence.evidence_text: The syllabus states that practical skills are acquired in labs and that the practical part is oriented toward Python with libraries including NumPy, Pandas, Requests, NLTK, spaCy, Gensim, fastText, SciPy, scikit-learn, TensorFlow, Keras, and PyTorch.

evidence.claim: The prerequisite profile requires programming, Python, and mathematical foundations.
evidence.source_title: Силабус Аналіз та обробка природньої мови (NLP) 2025.pdf
evidence.evidence_text: The prerequisite section explicitly names programming principles, algorithmization, Python syntax and data structures, OOP, IDE/environment work, probability, discrete mathematics, matrix theory, and analytic geometry.

evidence.claim: The lab track is progressive and implementation-heavy.
evidence.source_title: Силабус Аналіз та обробка природньої мови (NLP) 2025.pdf
evidence.evidence_text: The syllabus says lab tasks are divided by complexity levels and built on a principle of growing functionality across topics.

evidence.claim: Preprocessing is implemented as a concrete pipeline with persisted artifacts.
evidence.evidence_text: Lab 2 requires saving raw input, filtering data, normalizing it, applying tokenization by selected types, removing stop words, lemmatizing, stemming, finding top words, and storing results of each stage in separate files.

evidence.claim: Classification is taught as both supervised and unsupervised text categorization.
evidence.evidence_text: Lecture 8 defines text classification as assigning tags or categories to unstructured text and explicitly distinguishes supervised tag assignment from unsupervised category-based analysis.

evidence.claim: Similarity analysis includes embedding-based methods, not only basic lexical comparison.
evidence.evidence_text: Lecture 9 presents cosine similarity as well as BERT, SBERT, and the Universal Sentence Encoder for sentence or text similarity tasks.

evidence.claim: Sentiment analysis is treated as a practical text classification problem with multiple tool families.
evidence.evidence_text: Lecture 10 defines sentiment analysis as determining emotional tone and lists Python libraries, deep-learning frameworks, pretrained models, and cloud services for this task.

evidence.claim: Neural methods are introduced at the architecture and implementation levels.
evidence.evidence_text: Lecture 11 covers ANN methodology and main neural architectures for NLP, including FNN, RNN, LSTM, GRU, CNN, and Transformers.

evidence.claim: The neural-methods lab requires model selection and architecture-level design.
evidence.evidence_text: Lab 6 requires choosing or synthesizing a mathematical model and performing architecture design through a structural scheme, class diagram, or algorithm block diagram before implementation.
